verdict.why: The left build has layered massing (mossy stone plinth, timber-framed storeys with white plaster, a dark timber gallery band, and a teal roof), with lanterns and a readable door, so it reads as a lived-in building with character. The right build is a plain tapering shaft with a stepped cap and flat purple window patches that look pasted on rather than cut into the wall, so it reads more as a generic tower.
